questions.question: In a certain code language, 'He is my nephew’ is coded as 'Co Pv Zs Mn’, 'That is my car’ is coded as 'Zs Pt Pv Ga’, 'He is your uncle’ is coded as 'Co Pv Ex Yz'. What is the code for ‘nephew’ in this code language?
questions.solution:
Given:

'He is my nephew’ is coded as 'Co Pv Zs Mn’

'That is my car’ is coded as 'Zs Pt Pv Ga’

'He is your uncle’ is coded as 'Co Pv Ex Yz'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a2a52d90cc2ce9e66b7fdbb069837e413b5d8c65c16b0faf3e87e6c9e44f0d21.png] 

Here,

'Mn' is the code for 'Nephew'.

'Zs' is the code for 'my'.

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All Z are Y.

II. Some Y are B.

**Conclusion:**

I. Some B are not Z.

II. Some Y are not Z.

III. Some Z are Y.

options.text: Both conclusions II and III follows
Both conclusions I and III follows

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

I. All Z are Y.

II. Some Y are B.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1666625056af75bac98abf2c9468dcd942af7b55207afed6385d81c462d55121.png] 

Conclusions:

Conclusion I: **False** ("Some B are not Z" is not true because there is no negative relation between B and Z. It may be possible but not definitely true. In syllogism, we take the definite cases as true. So this conclusion not follow.)

Conclusion II: **False** ("Some Y are not Z" is not true because there is no negative relation between Y and Z. It may be possible but not definitely true. So, this conclusion also not follow.)

Conclusion III: **True** ("Some Z are Y" is true because when all Z are Y is given then "some Z are Y" is also true. Please note that "some" is a subset of "all". For example, when all boys are male, then "some boys are male" is also true.) 

So, Only conclusion III follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__****Negative Conclusions will never be definitely true when a given statement is positive.

Here, Conclusion I & II is negative, so it will be true in possibility only.**

questions.question:
By Interchanging the given two numbers which of the following equation will be correct? 

1 and 6

I. 7 - 5 + 1 × 3 ÷ 6 = 20

II. 1 × 7 + 6 - 4 ÷ 2 = 40
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50192f098c21078501d30eeafe1a8c64bc30dd9621c48caa8a39ffc60f68b64.png] 

Given equation I. 7 - 5 + 1 × 3 ÷ 6 = 20

Now, if '1 and 6' are interchanged, then:

⇒ 7 - 5 + 6 × __**3 ÷ 1**__ = 20

⇒ 7 - 5 + __**6 × 3**__ = 20

⇒ __**7**__ - 5 __**+ 18**__ = 20

⇒ __25 - 5__ = 20

⇒ 20 = 20

LHS = RHS.

Given equation II: 1 × 7 + 6 - 4 ÷ 2 = 40

Now, if '1 and 6' are interchanged, then:

⇒ 6 × 7 + 1 - __**4 ÷ 2**__ = 40

⇒ __**6 × 7**__ + 1 - 2 = 40

⇒ __**42 + 1**__ - 2 = 40

⇒ __43 - 2__ = 40

⇒ 41 ≠ 40

LHS ≠ RHS.

Here, Only Equation I are the correct after interchanging the given symbol.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question:
Select the option in which the numbers shares the same relationship in set as that shared by the numbers in the given set. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13-Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

(8, 27, 125)

(64, 1331, 1728)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **All the numbers are perfect cube.**

Now,

**For, (8, 27, 125)**

**⇒ 8 = Cube of 2.**

**⇒ 27 = Cube of 3.**

**⇒ 125 = Cube of 5.**

**For, (64, 1331, 1728)**

**⇒ 64 = Cube of 4.**

**⇒ 1331 = Cube of 11.**

**⇒ 1728 = Cube of 12.**

Now checking the options,

Option 1) (289, 212, 196) 

⇒ 289 = Not a Cube number.

⇒ 212 = Not a Cube number.

⇒ 196 = Not a Cube number.

Option 2) (200, 215, 256) 

⇒ 200 = Not a Cube number.

⇒ 215 = Not a Cube number.

⇒ 256 = Not a Cube number.

Option 3) (125, 172, 144) 

⇒ 125 = Cube of 5.

⇒ 172 = Not a Cube number.

⇒ 144 = Not a Cube number.

Option 4) **(216, 343, 512) **

**⇒ 216 = Cube of 6.**

**⇒ 343 = Cube of 7.**

**⇒ 512 = Cube of 8.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question: In a certain code language. 'APPLE’ is written as '25' and 'JUNIOR' is written as '36', How will 'PACKAGE' be written in that language?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b1ef5af07dc7cdface0347994bbc6f824cbda2bac27bcab0cb4cf07968dfa00.png] 

The logic followed here is:

Logic: (Number of letters)².

Now,

'APPLE’ is written as '25'

⇒ Number of letters in 'APPLE' = 5

⇒ 5² = 25.

For, 'JUNIOR' is written as '36'

⇒ Number of letters in 'JUNIOR' = 6

⇒ 62 = 36.

Similarly, for ‘**PACKAGE**’

⇒ **Number of letters in 'PACKAGE' = 7**

**⇒ 72 = 49.**

So, 'PACKAGE' will be written as '49'.

Hence, the correct answer is "49".

questions.question:
By Interchanging which two signs the equation will be correct? 

15 + 5 ÷ 2 - 9 × 3 = 22
questions.solution:
Given equation: 15 + 5 ÷ 2 - 9 × 3 = 22.

BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50192f098c21078501d30eeafe1a8c64bc30dd9621c48caa8a39ffc60f68b64.png] 

Let's check each option one by one.

Option 1) + and -

Given: 15 + 5 ÷ 2 - 9 × 3 = 22

After interchanging the numbers we get;

⇒ 15 - __**5 ÷ 2**__ + 9 × 3 = 22

⇒ 15 - 2.5 + __**9 × 3**__ = 22

⇒ __**15**__ - 2.5 __**+ 27**__ = 22

⇒ __42 - 2.5__ = 22

⇒ 39.5 ≠ 22

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

**Option 2) × and ÷ **

Given: 15 + 5 ÷ 2 - 9 × 3 = 22

After interchanging the numbers we get;

⇒ 15 + 5 × 2 - __**9 ÷ 3**__ = 22

⇒ 15 + __**5 × 2**__ - 3 = 22

⇒ __**15 + 10**__ - 3 = 22

⇒ __25** - 3**__ = 22

⇒ **22 = 22**

**⇒ LHS = RHS**

Option 3) × and +

Given: 15 + 5 ÷ 2 - 9 × 3 = 22

After interchanging the numbers we get;

⇒ 15 × __**5 ÷ 2**__ - 9 + 3 = 22

⇒ __**15 × 2.5**__ - 9 + 3 = 22

⇒ __**37.5**__ - 9 __**+ 3**__ = 22

⇒ __40.5 - 9__ = 22

⇒ 31.5 ≠ 22

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) ÷ and +

Given: 15 + 5 ÷ 2 - 9 × 3 = 22

After interchanging the numbers we get;

⇒ __**15 ÷ 5**__ + 2 - 9 × 3 = 22

⇒ 3 + 2 - __**9 × 3**__ = 22

⇒ __**3 + 2**__ - 27 = 22

⇒ __5____ - 27__ = 22

⇒ -22 ≠ 22

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".
